title: Project Journey
subtitle: How a browser-only, on-device voice studio was built — the engineering problems, the decisions, and the measurements behind them.
scope: This is an engineering history of integrating and optimising existing open TTS models (ZipVoice-Distill, Chatterbox, F5-TTS) for in-browser inference. We did not create these models. Every number below comes from a measurement recorded in the repository; each comparison states its conditions. Unless noted: Apple M5 Pro (25.8 GB), macOS, Chrome 156.0.8078.48, assets served from a local static server (no Internet download time).

milestones.title: Can a whole TTS model run inside a browser tab?
milestones.problem: Before any product work: can text → speech with voice cloning, in Mandarin and English, run entirely inside a web page, with no inference server?
milestones.why: Start from the smallest proven artefact: the static k2-fsa ZipVoice Space, which ships ZipVoice-Distill compiled to WebAssembly via sherpa-onnx. Drive it unmodified with our own minimal page so any result is attributable to the runtime, not to our code.
what: Minimal site on the upstream sherpa-onnx WASM runtime (text front end, encoder, 4-step decoder and vocoder all inside one Web Worker)
Static file server with the cross-origin isolation headers the runtime needs
evidence: Inference observed fully in-tab: the only network requests were to localhost
English, Mandarin and code-switched outputs intelligible to Whisper-small (ASR checks intelligibility only)

metrics.label: Warm generation speed (single-thread WASM, ~5 s of speech)

limitations: Not real-time and not streaming: audio exists only after the whole sentence is generated
Synthetic (macOS `say`) reference voices; speaker similarity not evaluated
Chinese text with an English reference was poor (ASR garbage)

milestones.title: ZipVoice WASM baseline: where does the time go?
milestones.problem: The in-browser model was 2–3× slower than real time. Was that the thread count, the model, or the runtime?
milestones.why: Measure before optimising: run the exact same model files natively (sherpa-onnx / ONNX Runtime CPU) and in Chrome, with the same thread count and inputs, so the comparison isolates the runtime.
what: Profiling instrumentation in the browser worker
Browser and native benchmark harnesses (153 recorded runs)
Step-count sweep to split fixed cost from per-decoder-step cost
evidence: ≈ 95 % of the time is the flow-matching decoder (fixed cost ≈ 0.4 s in WASM)
1 → 4 native threads gives only ≈ 1.6×; the browser build is single-threaded anyway

metrics.label: Same model, same 1 thread, 4 steps, Mandarin text

limitations: The browser stage split is a regression estimate (the WASM API exposes no per-stage timers)
One machine, one browser

milestones.title: ZipVoice on the GPU: a hybrid WebGPU + WASM pipeline
milestones.problem: Moving the decoder to WebGPU looked obvious, but the shipped INT8 decoder uses MatMulInteger / DynamicQuantizeLinear, which ONNX Runtime Web's WebGPU backend cannot run: 2,254 nodes fell back to the CPU and it got slower (2,941 vs 2,750 ms per step).
milestones.why: Keep the model's own weights and change only how they are executed: rewrite each INT8 MatMul chain into an FP32 MatMul over the dequantised weights (nothing retrained), run that decoder on WebGPU, and keep the text front end, encoder and vocoder in WebAssembly where they are cheap.
what: INT8 → FP32 decoder rewrite (478 MB `decoder.dq.fp32.onnx`)
Patched sherpa-onnx WASM exposing prepare / vocode / seed so the decoder can run outside it
Automatic fallback to the WASM baseline when WebGPU or the decoder is unavailable, always with a visible notice
evidence: Decoder output matches native to relative L2 ≈ 7e-7
Same seed → bit-identical audio (log-mel distance 0.000)
FP32-WebGPU vs INT8-WASM difference was 1.9–5.9× smaller than ordinary seed-to-seed variation (a crude numerical metric, not perception)
Fault injection: no WebGPU and blocked decoder download both fall back correctly

metrics.label: English sentence (≈ 8 s of speech), same recording and text, 4 steps, warm
Mandarin sentence (≈ 10.6 s of speech), same conditions

limitations: Nobody has yet listened to compare GPU and CPU outputs
Extra 478 MB download on first use
Still full-utterance output, not streaming

milestones.title: One page, three models
milestones.problem: Chatterbox (English, expressive) and F5-TTS (Mandarin + English) were each proven in their own proof-of-concept page. Comparing them with ZipVoice required one consistent environment.
milestones.why: A single adapter contract — load, generate, unload — with one Web Worker per model, so models can be switched without sharing runtime state, and a headless regression runner that exercises them all through the same UI.
what: Chatterbox browser PoC (Transformers.js + ONNX Runtime Web, WebGPU)
F5-TTS browser PoC with an in-browser pinyin front end for Mandarin
Unified playground with per-model adapters and a muted, headless regression runner
evidence: Interleaved four-adapter regression in one page: 12/12 cases pass, no leaks between models
Automated runs never autoplay
limitations: F5 timings recorded before the sampling fix (next milestone) are invalid
Quality judged by ASR only at this stage

milestones.title: F5-TTS: correcting the sampling schedule
milestones.problem: F5 English sounded noisy at the default step settings — heard by the project owner, invisible to ASR. The exported transformer has a 32-point sway-sampling schedule baked in; our loop walked NFE−1 consecutive points, so at NFE 16 the ODE stopped at t = 0.275 instead of t = 1, leaving a noise-dominated mel spectrogram.
milestones.why: This is an implementation correction of the sampler loop for this ONNX export, not a new algorithm: select NFE−1 of the baked time points and rescale each step's update by (interval dt) / (baked dt), so every setting integrates the whole trajectory. NFE 32 is the unmodified baked schedule.
what: Corrected Euler plan with ODE end-time reporting (must be 1.000)
35 schedule unit tests and browser regression cases
A negative control that still detects the original truncated trajectory
evidence: Every NFE ends at t = 1.000
Mel standard deviation ≈ 2.8 after vs 1.05 with the bug
Listening check passed: the project owner accepted English outputs at NFE 12, 16 and 32 (F5 test build, 2026-10-22)
limitations: A subset-of-grid approximation, not identical to F5's own N-step schedule (the export cannot embed other time points)
Mandarin and mixed-language quality: automated checks only, no listening yet

milestones.title: Your own voice: guided microphone recording
milestones.problem: Zero-shot cloning is only meaningful with the user's own voice, and ZipVoice and F5 need the exact words of that recording. Uploads and built-in default voices distracted from that.
milestones.why: Guide the user to read a short passage, so the transcript is known exactly (it is the passage) and can still be corrected. Capture raw audio, without the browser's echo cancellation, noise suppression or gain control, to keep the timbre.
what: Passages in English and Taiwan Traditional Chinese; transcript filled automatically
Raw mono Float32 capture through an AudioWorklet; checks for too short, silent or clipped recordings
Microphone-only public page; uploads and default voices moved to a research page for regression tooling
evidence: Tests assert that only same-origin requests with empty bodies are made — the recording never leaves the tab
Playback only on a button press
limitations: Automated tests use Chrome's fake microphone (a synthetic voice)
Speaker similarity with real voices not measured objectively

milestones.title: Local-first assets and strict offline inference
milestones.problem: A demo must not depend on a CDN or on Hugging Face being reachable, and it must be provable that no audio or text leaves the device.
milestones.why: Serve every model file and JavaScript library from the same site, check them at startup, and test with all non-local requests blocked.
what: Asset manifest and startup preflight (missing files are named, with the fix)
Vendored libraries and local F5 weights
Strict-offline regression: a fresh profile with every external request blocked
evidence: Strict offline: all four model routes generate audio with 0 external requests
limitations: First visit still has to download ≈ 3 GB of model files from this site; Internet download time was never measured

milestones.title: Background preload and resident models
milestones.problem: A real user saw Chatterbox load in 43.8 s, then again in 47.9 s. Switching models threw the loaded one away, so returning to Chatterbox paid the whole initialisation again.
milestones.why: Measure the lifecycle first (every worker, load, unload and generate is recorded), then keep up to two models loaded, evicting the one that is cheapest to reload, and start loading as soon as the user confirms a model, while they type and record.
what: Residency policy: at most 2 resident models (1 on low-memory devices), cost-aware eviction
Background preload after the model is chosen (never while just browsing)
Truthful load reporting: 'already loaded' vs 'waited X s'
evidence: Same model again, or switching away and back: 0 workers created, 0 loads, 0 bytes fetched
Memory measured per resident model (physical footprint incl. GPU): Chatterbox +2.0 GB, ZipVoice hybrid +2.7 GB, F5 +2.9 GB

metrics.label: Chatterbox, switch away and back, then Generate

limitations: The first initialisation itself was still ≈ 37–39 s (solved two milestones later)
Residency is bounded by memory

milestones.title: Four scenes: one question at a time
milestones.problem: The playground looked like a research dashboard: every control on one page, technical words up front.
milestones.why: Ask one question per scene — model, message, voice, generate — with motion that explains where you are, while keeping every measurement available in an Advanced sheet.
what: Scene engine with View Transitions and a shared-element model indicator
Viewport-fitted layouts, keyboard and IME rules, reduced-motion support
Language-aware reference recommendation; reference approval per model and language
Honest progress: F5 shows real sampling steps, never a fake percentage
evidence: Scene 2 refinement and F5 progress accepted by the project owner (commit 60add8f)
UX regression suite: 113/113 checks at the start of Voice Studio 2.0
limitations: Visual judgement from screenshots and the owner's review; other browsers not tested

milestones.title: Why does Chatterbox take 38 seconds to start?
milestones.problem: Even with every file already on the computer, Chatterbox took ≈ 38 s to become ready on every page load.
milestones.why: Instrument before guessing: time each ONNX session, trace the worker thread, then reproduce the slow session natively and sample its stack.
what: Per-session profiler in the worker
Isolated single-session benchmark across runtimes and options
Native reproduction with ONNX Runtime 1.31 and stack sampling
evidence: One session — the 23,934-node conditional_decoder — took 35.6–36.0 s; the other three ≈ 1 s together
Not network, cache, GPU upload or shader compilation: CPU work inside ONNX Runtime on the worker thread
Native verbose log: 24.4 s of 25.8 s in ONNX Runtime's execution/memory allocation planning
Natively, memory reuse off: 25.7 s → 1.48 s, with bitwise-identical output on a seeded test copy

metrics.label: conditional_decoder session, native ONNX Runtime CPU

limitations: ONNX Runtime Web offered no switch for this option

milestones.title: A 10-line ONNX Runtime patch, one session only
milestones.problem: The browser runtime had no way to turn off memory-reuse planning, and turning it off for every model would change behaviour that was not broken.
milestones.why: Add one opt-in session configuration key (`session.disable_mem_reuse`) to ONNX Runtime, rebuild only its WebAssembly from the exact commit Transformers.js uses, and set the key on the Chatterbox decoder session alone. Default behaviour for everything else is unchanged.
what: 10-line patch + pinned, reproducible build script
Decoder-only session option in the Chatterbox worker
evidence: Native stack sampling: 94 % of the slow phase inside PlannerImpl::FindReusableTensor (memory-reuse planning), which scans every free buffer for every value of a 24k-node graph
Seeded decoder test: bitwise-identical waveforms, original vs patched runtime
42 full-pipeline generations: Whisper transcript exact for all
Listening comparison passed (project owner, normal Chrome, 2026-10-25): comparable naturalness, intelligibility and speaker similarity; no noise, clipping or silence

metrics.label: Chatterbox model ready, page reload, median of 5 (experiment branch)

limitations: A custom runtime build to maintain whenever Transformers.js updates ONNX Runtime
The option is not upstream (yet)

milestones.title: Fast Chatterbox in the product, with a safe fallback
milestones.problem: Bring the validated patch into the four-scene app without risking a broken runtime for users.
milestones.why: Runtime selection before the first session: use the patched build if it is present and matches the expected ONNX Runtime commit; otherwise — or if it fails — recreate the worker with the standard runtime and record why. Never label a standard run as patched.
what: auto / patched / stock runtime selection (developer option) with verified fallback
Fresh-clone rebuild of the runtime
CPU path verified in a browser without WebGPU
evidence: Integrated benchmark, 5 page reloads each: ready 38.37 s → 3.77 s (×10.2)
Warm inference unchanged: RTF 0.58 → 0.59
Perceived wait at Generate for a quick user: 31.2 s → 0 s
No-WebGPU browser: Chatterbox ran on its CPU device with the patched runtime

metrics.label: Chatterbox model ready, page reload, median of 5 (integrated app)
metrics.note: initialisation only — not 10× faster speech generation

limitations: Generation speed varies with the recording and sentence: real-user runs with an 11.1 s microphone recording measured RTF 1.94 and 1.07 (docs/chatterbox_lifecycle.md), and the owner reported a real-microphone run at RTF 2.01 (3.32 s of speech in 6.69 s); the controlled benchmark sentence gives ≈ 0.58
Outputs of the integrated app not yet individually listened to

milestones.title: F5 background preload on a fresh browser profile
milestones.problem: On a first visit F5's background preload started on time but failed half a second later (a Cache Storage write error, then a failed read of the downloaded data), so the user waited at Generate instead.
milestones.why: Files served by this site are already local: stop duplicating them into Cache Storage, join the downloaded chunks in memory, and never let a failed cache write abort the load.
what: Robust download path in the F5 worker (inference unchanged)
evidence: Three fresh-profile runs: F5 ready in 1.0–1.1 s, before Generate, 0 s wait
The same failure reproduced on the previous build, so it was pre-existing
limitations: Root cause inside Chrome's Cache Storage not investigated further

milestones.title: Voice Studio 2.0: compare, keep, explain
milestones.problem: Comparing models meant recording and typing everything again for each one; results disappeared after the next generation; and the evidence above lived only in documents.
milestones.why: One shared generation pipeline for every feature, so Compare and My creations reuse the same adapters, preload and residency rules — no second inference path.
what: Model cards that say what each model is good at and where it is limited, with live readiness and a Learn more sheet
Compare: the same message and voice across models, run one after another, with real measurements and blind listening
My creations: replay, download, reuse, generate again, send to Compare; optional storage on this device
Separate Advanced settings and Developer diagnostics; one clear generation status
evidence: Full regression after the change: UX 113/113, recording 51/51, Chatterbox runtime 13/13 (incl. a browser without WebGPU), interleaved 9/9, strict offline 5/5 with 0 external requests, Voice Studio checks 67/67
A three-model comparison of one English sentence: ZipVoice 1.06 s, Chatterbox 2.80 s, F5 5.90 s of generation (single runs; not a ranking)
Three consecutive comparisons in one page: live workers always equal the resident models; browser footprint flat at 3.2–3.4 GB
limitations: Blind listening notes are personal impressions, not a MOS study
A generation already running inside a model cannot be cancelled; Compare stops between models
Human listening of this build not done yet

milestones.title: A public website: GitHub Pages + the models' own Hugging Face repositories
milestones.problem: The demo had to work for anyone with a link, with the project computer switched off, on free hosting, without re-uploading gigabytes of other people's model weights.
milestones.why: GitHub Pages serves only the app (≈ 124 MB of static files); the browser downloads the model weights directly from the original Hugging Face repositories at pinned revisions. The one file we derived (the 478 MB FP32 ZipVoice decoder) is rebuilt in the browser from the INT8 decoder it already downloads.
what: Every hosted model file checked against the Hub at its pinned revision (size + sha256) on each build; the service worker checks sha256 again before keeping a copy
ZipVoice WebGPU decoder: a 4.2 MB weight-free graph + a 24 KB recipe replace the 478 MB file; weights rebuilt and sha256-checked in about 0.6 s
Works under a sub-path (/VoiceStudio/); the CSP allows this site and Hugging Face only; no request leaves the page before a model is used
evidence: Rebuilt decoder weights byte-identical to the original; decoder outputs bit-identical on WebGPU (3 input shapes, max difference 0) and on ORT CPU

Fresh browser profile against a local GitHub Pages stand-in with real Hugging Face downloads: all three models generated real audio (ZipVoice zh/en on WebGPU, Chatterbox en with the patched runtime, F5 en/zh at NFE 12/16/32 ending at t = 1)
Reload: no model file downloaded again; offline (network off, and whole page reloaded offline): all three models still generate
Chatterbox model-ready from saved files: 5.2 s with the patched runtime vs 56.0 s stock (×10.7, 2 runs each)

metrics.label: ZipVoice first-use download
metrics.note: FP32 decoder rebuilt in the browser instead of downloaded

limitations: Measured on one machine (Apple M5 Pro, Chrome 156, headless); other browsers, phones and Windows not tested
Depends on the upstream Hugging Face repositories keeping these revisions available
Interrupted downloads restart the file from the beginning
